message.content:
Logistic regression predicts a probability between 0 and 1 for each observation.  
A linear combination of inputs feeds through a sigmoid curve so the result lies in that range.  
For two classes the predicted class is chosen when the probability exceeds ½.  
Coefficients show how much each predictor changes the odds of being in the positive group.  
Model fitting maximises likelihood rather than least‑squares error.  
Regularisation (L1/L2) helps prevent overfitting when predictors outnumber observations.
